scope: extension/ (Manifest V3 browser extension: background service worker, content scripts, UI, providers, storage, analysis pipeline, options page)
repository configuration, documentation and full Git history
methodology: Phase 1 - architecture and trust-boundary discovery from source and documentation
Phase 2 - attack-surface mapping: every extension message handler, network egress, storage access and rendering sink
Phase 3 - source-to-sink review of authentication/authorization, secrets, injection, XSS, browser security, logging, dependencies, deployment configuration and backup
Phase 4 - AI security review (prompt injection, sensitive disclosure, output handling, agency, tool/MCP, RAG/memory, resource abuse, AI supply chain)
Phase 5 - evidence-based classification (CONFIRMED vs VALIDATION REQUIRED vs NOT APPLICABLE vs NOT VERIFIABLE)
Phase 6 - coverage accounting and verification of security strengths
Static analysis with grep/ripgrep, byte-level comparison of vendored code, npm audit, git-history secret scanning, and targeted dynamic probes of the JavaScript modules in Node
No exploit was executed against a live browser; see limitations

not_applicable_categories: AUTHORIZATION / IDOR / TENANT ISOLATION (no accounts, no tenants, no server-side objects)
AUTHENTICATION (no login, session, token or webhook authentication; BYOK API key only)
CSRF (no cookies and no browser-automatically-attached credentials)
AI excessive agency, tool/MCP security, RAG/vector/memory security (no tools, no MCP, no RAG, no agents)
Infrastructure as Code, containers, Kubernetes, Terraform, reverse proxy, CI/CD privileges (none present)
not_verifiable_categories: Backup and recovery (no repository, IaC, automation or operational documentation provides evidence)
TLS termination, HSTS and transport hardening outside the extension (provider-side / OS-side)

stack.frontend: In-page UI injected by content scripts (closed Shadow DOM); extension options page in vanilla JS (ES module). No framework, no bundler, no build step.
stack.backend: None. No server, no database, no queue, no worker fleet.
stack.apis: 10 internal chrome.runtime message handlers (background) + 2 (content script). No public HTTP API.
stack.http_clients: globalThis.fetch, used from exactly one function (providers/common.js send)
stack.databases: chrome.storage.local only (settings, analysis cache, usage totals)
stack.authentication: None (no accounts). BYOK provider API key typed by the user on the options page.
stack.authorization: Sender-identity checks on every internal message (sender.id === chrome.runtime.id) plus per-handler context gates (isExtensionPage / isContentScript)
stack.tenancy_model: Single user, single browser profile. No tenants, workspaces or organizations.
stack.queues_workers: MV3 background service worker; no job queue
stack.secret_management: User-supplied API key in chrome.storage.local; not encrypted (documented in SECURITY.md / ADR-005)
stack.validation: Hand-written coercion + strict enum/clamping validator (analysis/validator.js); custom URL allow-list (providers/openai-compatible.js)
stack.ai_components: Single LLM text-completion call for article analysis. No tools, function calling, MCP, RAG, vector store, agents or long-term memory.

dependencies.lockfile: package-lock.json, lockfileVersion 3, 38 resolved packages, all registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity

architecture.data_flow: PAGE (untrusted DOM) -> content script: Readability on a clone -> normalize -> ArticleDocument (schema 1.0 + SHA-256) -> chrome.runtime message -> background service worker -> provider adapter -> LLM provider (HTTPS) -> untrusted JSON -> bounded read -> parseModelJson -> validateAnalysis (enum/clamp/cap, status derived) -> chrome.storage.local cache + reply -> content script -> in-page UI (textContent in a closed Shadow DOM)
trust_boundaries: webpage (untrusted) -> content-script isolated world: DOM, text, metadata, links; extraction on a clone; no HTML crosses
content script -> background: message payloads re-checked by articleDocumentProblem and per-handler sender gates
background -> provider: the only network egress; carries the API key; redirect:error, credentials:omit, 60 s timeout
provider -> background: untrusted body, capped at 2 MB, JSON-parsed defensively, key-redacted error text
chrome.storage.local -> background/options: re-validated on every read
validated result -> UI: text nodes only, closed Shadow DOM; page cannot read or script it

findings.title: API key is reachable from the content-script context through chrome.storage.local
findings.affected_component: Content-script execution context and the settings store

lines.extension/content/content-script.js: 1-14 (comment stating content scripts must never receive API keys)

findings.evidence:
manifest.json grants the extension-wide `storage` permission and injects content scripts into every http/https page:

  "permissions": [ "storage" ]
  "content_scripts": [{ "matches": ["http://*/*", "https://*/*"], ... }]

The settings store keeps the provider credential in that same, extension-wide area:

  const STORAGE_KEY = "settings";
  apiKey: str(src.apiKey),
  async get() { const stored = await area.get(STORAGE_KEY); return sanitizeSettings(...); }

Chrome exposes the chrome.storage API to content scripts whenever the extension holds the `storage` permission. The extension correctly never *sends* the key over the message channel (FACTIT_UI_PREFS returns only `{ language }`, verified at service-worker.js L151-156), but the credential remains reachable from the content-script execution context itself, which is the context that processes hostile page content and loads third-party code (extension/vendor/Readability.js).
findings.attack_path:
UNTRUSTED WEBPAGE CONTENT
-> vendored Readability / content-script code executes attacker-influenced input inside the isolated world
-> MISSING/BROKEN CONTROL: no per-context access control on chrome.storage.local for content scripts; the credential is stored where the least-trusted extension context can read it
-> chrome.storage.local.get("settings").apiKey
-> exfiltration to the page or to the network
-> IMPACT: disclosure of the user's provider API key (billing/abuse on the user's account)
preconditions: JavaScript execution inside the content script's isolated world (a memory-safety or logic bug in the content-script code or in a component loaded into it such as the vendored Readability). No such primitive was found in this repository.
The user has saved an API key.
findings.exploitability: This is recorded as VALIDATION REQUIRED and is NOT counted as a confirmed vulnerability. No code-execution primitive in the content-script world was identified, and Chrome's isolated world prevents the page from calling chrome.storage directly. The condition is nonetheless real and verifiable at runtime: the credential is stored in an area that a lower-trust context can read. It was not executed in a browser during this audit (see limitations), so the runtime reachability rests on documented platform behaviour plus the manifest permissions.
findings.impact: If the precondition is ever met, full provider API key disclosure, plus the article text that the script already handles. No account takeover of Fact It itself (there are no accounts).
findings.why_exploitable: Impact depends entirely on obtaining the precondition. Without it, the page cannot reach chrome.storage and cannot read the closed Shadow DOM. The finding is therefore a trust-boundary/defence-in-depth gap rather than an exploitable defect.
recommended_remediation: Record this explicitly in SECURITY.md's known-limitations section so the boundary statement ('content scripts must never receive API keys') matches the platform reality.
Keep the content-script world minimal and treat every library loaded into it (currently vendored Readability) as security-relevant; re-vendor only from integrity-verified packages (already done).

Evaluate storing the credential in a context that content scripts cannot read by default. chrome.storage.session is not exposed to content scripts unless setAccessLevel('TRUSTED_AND_UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS') is called; using it for the key, with the background worker re-hydrating it, would remove the content-script reachability at the cost of re-entry after browser restart (the tradeoff ADR-005 rejected - revisit it with this new information rather than silently).
Add a regression test that asserts content-script sources never import storage modules or reference chrome.storage.
verification_criteria: A documented decision exists in SECURITY.md / DECISIONS.md that states where the key is stored and whether content scripts can read it.

If the session-storage option is adopted: from a content-script isolated world, chrome.storage.local.get('settings') returns no apiKey and chrome.storage.session.get('settings') either returns nothing or throws, while the background worker can still complete an analysis.
If the risk is accepted instead: the acceptance is written down with the compensating controls.
A test fails if any file under extension/content/ gains a chrome.storage reference or imports storage/.

findings.title: Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint may be any remote https host, which then receives the API key and the article
findings.attack_path:
LOCAL USER (or a user socially engineered into pasting a hostile base URL)
-> options page writes settings.baseUrl via chrome.storage.local
-> validateBaseUrl (protocol / loopback / credentials / query / fragment checks pass)
-> MISSING/BROKEN CONTROL: no allow-list or explicit confirmation for non-loopback remote hosts
-> POST ${baseUrl}/chat/completions with 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' and the article JSON
-> IMPACT: the configured server receives the user's API key and the article being read
preconditions: The user deliberately configures a remote/https OpenAI-compatible base URL, or is persuaded to.
An API key is set (optional for this provider).
findings.exploitability: Not reachable by a webpage or by a remote attacker. The content script cannot write settings and cannot trigger provider calls: every privileged handler is gated (service-worker.js L126-192) and the repository's smoke test asserts that a content script calling FACTIT_TEST_PROVIDER is ignored and that an extension page calling FACTIT_ANALYZE is ignored. Exploitation requires the local user's own configuration action. Recorded for completeness of the custom-endpoint review, not as a defect.
findings.impact: Disclosure of the API key and of the analysed article to the configured endpoint; the impact is bounded by the provider's key permissions and by the spend limit the user is advised to set.
findings.why_exploitable: It is not exploitable without local user action. The residual risk is a trust decision, not a code flaw. The strong parts of the control (https except loopback, no credentials/query/fragment, redirect:error, credentials:omit, 2 MB cap) were verified in the source.
recommended_remediation: Optionally refuse or require an explicit confirmation for remote https hosts that resolve to private, loopback or link-local ranges (169.254.0.0/16, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, fc00::/7), since a legitimate remote Chat Completions server is rarely in those ranges.
Keep and surface the existing warning at the point of entry of the base URL, not only in SECURITY.md.
No change is required if the accepted-risk decision is recorded; the current documentation already discloses it.
verification_criteria: A decision (fix or accept) is recorded in DECISIONS.md.

If an allow-list is added: tests assert that http:// and https:// URLs pointing at private/link-local ranges are rejected or require confirmation, while http://localhost, http://127.0.0.1 and https://<public host> still work.
The settings page continues to warn before a non-loopback endpoint can be saved.

detail: FACTIT_PING (service-worker.js L131-133): any sender with sender.id === chrome.runtime.id; returns only {type, version}. Intentionally unauthenticated beyond sender identity. No privilege.
FACTIT_TEST_PROVIDER (L135-140): isExtensionPage only; spends tokens. Correct.
FACTIT_ANALYZE (L142-147): isContentScript only; spends tokens. Correct.
FACTIT_UI_PREFS (L151-156): isContentScript or isExtensionPage; returns only {language}. Correct - the key never leaves the privileged context.
FACTIT_LOOKUP (L158-163): isContentScript only; cache read keyed by a 64-hex hash; no token spend. Correct.
FACTIT_CACHE_STATS (L165-168): isExtensionPage only. Correct.
FACTIT_CACHE_CLEAR (L170-173): isExtensionPage only. Correct.
FACTIT_USAGE_STATS (L175-178): isExtensionPage only. Correct.
FACTIT_USAGE_RESET (L180-183): isExtensionPage only. Correct.
FACTIT_OPEN_SETTINGS (L185-188): isContentScript only. Correct.
FACTIT_EXTRACT (content-script.js L163-166): sender.id check. Correct.
FACTIT_TOGGLE (content-script.js L167-170): sender.id check. Correct.

authorization_gate_design.isExtensionPage (service-worker.js L53-6: requires sender.id === runtime.id, sender.url under the extension origin and sender.origin absent-or-matching. A content script always reports the http(s) page URL, so it can never pass.
authorization_gate_design.isContentScript (service-worker.js L66-7: requires sender.id === runtime.id, a tab, a tab id and an http(s) sender.url. Extension pages cannot pass.
authorization_gate_design.frontend_privilege_gates: None exist and none are relied upon. The options page performs no privileged action that the background does not re-check; there is no isAdmin/role/canEdit/canDelete pattern anywhere in the codebase.

sources_reviewed: full Git history (all revisions, added-file diffs)
notes: No .env files, no private keys, no cloud credentials, no service-account files, no OAuth secrets, no webhook secrets, no JWT signing secrets.
The only key-like strings are obvious test fixtures: 'sk-smoke-test-key-0000' (tests/integration/smoke.mjs L255, L280) and 'sk-abcdefghijklmnop' (tests/unit/providers.test.js L208).
dist/ and node_modules/ are untracked (.gitignore), and git ls-files confirms no build output is committed.
No insecure ${SECRET:-default} pattern exists; there is no server startup path.

Redaction (providers/common.js redact) removes the exact key plus sk-/key-/token- and Bearer patterns from every provider error surface. Verified by targeted execution: exact, URL-encoded and sk--prefixed echoes are redacted; a case-mutated echo of a prefix-less key is not (residual, informational - the error text is only shown to the local user who already owns the key).

input_validation_and_injection.raw_sql: None - no database and no query builder.
input_validation_and_injection.shell_execution: None in the extension. Build scripts use execFileSync with fixed argument arrays (scripts/package.mjs L18, L26).
input_validation_and_injection.path_traversal: None - filenames are constants. scripts/make-icons.mjs derives an icon size from the request query with Number(...) and falls back to 128, so no string injection into the served HTML.
input_validation_and_injection.unsafe_deserialization: JSON.parse only, of size-capped bodies; no eval, no new Function, no dynamic import of untrusted input.
input_validation_and_injection.ssrf: One egress point. Two hardcoded https endpoints; the third is the user-configured base URL validated by validateBaseUrl (see SEC-CHAIN-001). Not reachable from page content.
input_validation_and_injection.open_redirect: None - no redirect handling; fetch uses redirect:'error'.
input_validation_and_injection.header_injection: The model name and provider strings are placed in JSON bodies, not headers; header values come from settings and are rejected by fetch if malformed. No user-controlled value reaches a header beyond the API key.
input_validation_and_injection.prototype_pollution: Verified by execution: parseModelJson + validateAnalysis + migrateLegacy + migrate20 + sanitizeSettings with __proto__/constructor payloads leave Object.prototype untouched and produce no own __proto__ key.
input_validation_and_injection.oversized_input: Content capped at 40,000 chars and refused above that (engine.js articleDocumentProblem); prompt envelope re-bounds every field; provider response capped at 2 MB; 60 s abort timeout; DOM node cap of 60,000 before cloning.
input_validation_and_injection.redos: Timed hostile inputs against Intl.getCanonicalLocales and Date.parse (1-5 MB strings): all under 20 ms. No catastrophic backtracking found.

detail: No innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, createContextualFragment, srcdoc, eval, new Function or dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere in extension/ excluding vendor/.

Every dynamic value in ui/top-bar.js and ui/panel.js goes through a local el() helper that assigns textContent, or through document.createTextNode; the i18n interpolator t() returns a plain string that is only ever assigned to textContent.
The bar and panel live in a closed Shadow DOM (top-bar.js L103-107), so page CSS cannot restyle and page scripts cannot read the analysis.
Model-derived strings are additionally schema-bounded before rendering (validator.js: enum enforcement, clamping, per-field caps).
The README/development task link uses rel="noopener noreferrer" (options.html L28).

Rendering sinks reviewed: renderSummary, renderDetail, renderOverviewTab, renderClaimsTab, renderEvidenceTab, renderFramingTab, renderAboutTab, renderClaim, twoBoxesEl, tagChip, legend, closeButton, and top-bar setIdle/setLoading/setNoArticle/setResult/setError. All 17 apply text-node rendering.

browser_security.authentication_model: No cookies and no browser-automatically-attached credentials are used, so CSRF is NOT APPLICABLE. chrome.storage is not sent automatically by the browser.
browser_security.cors: Extension fetch uses credentials:'omit' and no cookies; no Access-Control headers are set by the extension.
browser_security.csp: No content_security_policy override; the Manifest V3 default (script-src 'self'; object-src 'self') applies to the options page. tests/unit/manifest.test.js asserts the options page uses no inline scripts or inline event handlers.
browser_security.web_accessible_resources: None declared, so no extension resource is reachable from web pages.
browser_security.externally_connectable: Not declared, so no external web page can message the extension.
browser_security.clickjacking: Extension pages are not web-accessible and Chrome blocks framing them. The in-page bar can be covered or imitated by the page, which SECURITY.md documents as an inherent limitation; the toolbar button re-asserts the real bar.
browser_security.cookies_samesite_secure_httponly: Not applicable - the extension sets no cookies.
browser_security.hsts_tls: NOT VERIFIABLE from the repository - TLS for api.openai.com / api.anthropic.com and any custom endpoint is terminated outside the extension.

detail: No console statement anywhere in extension/ references settings or the API key.
Content-script logging is limited to a fixed article summary (title/author/date/language/char counts/hash), the analysis result object, and error messages. Article body text is never logged.
Errors crossing back to the content script are normalised by errorDetail() (service-worker.js L77-80): only ProviderError/AnalysisError are serialised, everything else becomes a generic message.

Security-relevant events for an account-based system (login failures, privilege changes) do not exist here because there are no accounts or roles. The token-spending events are logged: 'analysis requested', 'analysis (…, cached) status=…', 'cached analysis found'.

supply_chain.lockfile: package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3), all 38 resolved URLs on registry.npmjs.org, all with sha512 integrity
supply_chain.install_scripts: None defined in package.json; dependencies are test-only and never shipped in extension/
supply_chain.vendored_code: extension/vendor/Readability.js and Readability-readerable.js are byte-identical to @mozilla/readability@0.6.0 (verified with diff: zero differing lines). tests/unit/vendor.test.js enforces this in CI-equivalent form.
supply_chain.ci_cd_actions: None - no .github/ or other CI configuration present
supply_chain.update_path: scripts/vendor-readability.mjs copies from the pinned node_modules package and refuses drift via tests

deployment_configuration.detail: No Dockerfile, docker-compose, Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, Terraform, Ansible, reverse-proxy configuration or CI/CD pipeline exists in the repository. There is no debug-mode flag, no management interface, no privileged container and no environment separation to review. The extension runs only in the user's browser profile.
manifest_hardening_reviewed: permissions: ["storage"] only; no host_permissions, no optional_permissions, no tabs, no activeTab, no scripting
content_scripts restricted to http://*/* and https://*/* (not <all_urls>), so file:// and other schemes are excluded

backup_recovery.detail: No backup, snapshot, export or restore mechanism is defined in code, IaC, automation or operational documentation. The only persisted state is a disposable analysis cache and usage counters in chrome.storage.local, plus the settings; loss of the browser profile loses at most the cache and requires re-entering the key. This is not recorded as a vulnerability.

ai_security.flow: MODEL (provider) <- SYSTEM PROMPT + USER TURN (article as a JSON data envelope) ; MODEL -> response text -> parseModelJson -> validateAnalysis -> AnalysisResult -> UI text. There is no retrieval, memory, tool, MCP or agent stage.
ai_security.prompt_injection: The article is transmitted as a JSON-stringified object inside the user turn, never concatenated into the system prompt; JSON escaping prevents the article from terminating the envelope or introducing structure. The system prompt explicitly classifies everything in the user message as data and instructs the model not to follow embedded instructions. Residual: an article can still attempt to steer the analysis outcome (this is inherent to analysing adversarial text). Impact is bounded because model output cannot trigger any privileged action - it is schema-validated and rendered as inert text. The product labels every result 'AI preliminary'. No confirmed vulnerability.
ai_security.sensitive_information_disclosure: No secrets are placed in prompts. The system prompt is public source, treated as public, not as a security boundary. Article text, title, author, date, language, up to 20 http(s) links and the page URL are sent to the user's chosen provider - disclosed in PRIVACY.md and on the settings page. Single-user extension: no cross-user or cross-tenant context exists.
ai_security.improper_output_handling: Model output is treated as untrusted end to end: balanced-brace JSON extraction, strict validation, per-field caps, enum enforcement, forced schema_version / verification_level / external_verification, and status recomputed by deriveStatus rather than taken from the model. Output reaches only text nodes. No shell, SQL, filesystem, code, URL or API sink is reachable from model output.
ai_security.excessive_agency: NOT APPLICABLE - the model has no tools, no function calling, no filesystem, no network and no decision authority. It returns text only.
ai_security.tool_mcp_security: NOT APPLICABLE - no tools, no MCP servers or clients, no tool descriptions or metadata.
ai_security.rag_memory_security: NOT APPLICABLE - no vector store, no retrieval, no embeddings, no long-term memory. The only persistence is a local analysis cache keyed by the SHA-256 of the article text, re-validated on every read.
ai_security.resource_abuse: No automatic provider call: analysis runs only on an explicit 'Analyze' click (ADR-006, enforced by the absence of automatic runAnalysis calls and asserted by the smoke test). One bounded retry on transient statuses; max_tokens 8192; 60 s timeout; 2 MB response cap; 40,000-char article cap; 200-entry LRU cache; cumulative usage counters with a reset. No recursive or unbounded loop exists. Denial-of-wallet requires repeated user clicks.
ai_security.ai_supply_chain: One model provider per request, chosen by the user; no model weights, adapters or plugins are shipped or downloaded. No third-party agent framework.

security_strengths.evidence: Every provider request flows through providers/common.js send(); the only fetch call in the extension (L59). Two adapters use hardcoded https endpoints; the third uses a validated user URL.

The key is read only by the background worker and the options page. FACTIT_UI_PREFS returns only { language } (service-worker.js L151-156); the options page never writes the stored key back into the form and shows a boolean 'hasStoredKey' instead (options.js L104-112).
providers/common.js redact() strips the exact key plus sk-/key-/token- and Bearer patterns and caps messages at 200 chars; verified by execution against exact, URL-encoded and prefixed echoes.
send() uses redirect:'error' and credentials:'omit' (common.js L64-68), so a hostile endpoint cannot bounce the credential to a third origin or harvest cookies.
permissions: ["storage"] only; no host_permissions, no web_accessible_resources, no externally_connectable; content scripts limited to http/https. Enforced by tests/unit/manifest.test.js.

All 12 message handlers check sender.id === chrome.runtime.id and 11 additionally require the correct context (isExtensionPage / isContentScript). The browser sets sender.url/origin, so a web page cannot forge them.

security_strengths.control: Untrusted input bounded at every hop
security_strengths.evidence: DOM node cap before cloning (extractor.js L99), 40,000-char content cap (normalize.js L53-57), prompt re-coercion of every field (prompt.js L61-77), 2 MB response cap (common.js L19, L125-150), 60 s timeout, 8192 max tokens.

security_strengths.control: Model output never trusted for control decisions
security_strengths.evidence: validator.js forces schema_version, verification_level and external_verification, derives status from concerns only (deriveStatus L233-238), clamps confidence, enforces enums and caps every string; prototype-pollution attempts are inert.
No HTML sink exists in extension/ outside vendor/. All model-derived text is assigned through textContent/createTextNode, inside a closed Shadow DOM (top-bar.js L103-107, panel.js L114-119).

security_strengths.control: Integrity-pinned supply chain and vendored code
security_strengths.evidence: 38/38 packages resolved from registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities; the vendored Readability is byte-identical to the pinned package and a test fails on drift.

security_strengths.control: Adversarial test coverage as executable security documentation
security_strengths.evidence: tests/unit/security.test.js contains 13 adversarial tests mapped to the SECURITY.md threat table; the full suite is 151 tests, all green (npm test).
SECURITY.md, PRIVACY.md, ADR-005 and the settings page state that chrome.storage.local is unencrypted, that a custom endpoint receives the key and article, and that the in-page UI can be spoofed.

limitations: This audit is of the repository at commit f69ddd8 (main), working tree clean. No live deployment was assessed.

No live browser execution was possible in the audit environment: the available Chromium build is snap-confined and fails to start, and the available Google Chrome (154) ignores --load-extension, so npm run test:smoke and the ad-hoc content-script storage probe could not be executed. Runtime claims that rest on browser behaviour (notably SEC-SECRETS-001 and the Chrome semantics of chrome.storage for content scripts) are therefore based on the manifest, the source and documented platform behaviour, and are marked VALIDATION REQUIRED.
The 151-test unit suite was executed successfully in Node (jsdom), including the adversarial security tests and the byte-for-byte vendor comparison.
Provider-side and network-side controls (TLS configuration, HSTS, provider rate limiting and abuse protection) are outside the repository and were not assessed.
No penetration test, fuzzing campaign or reverse engineering of the browser runtime was performed.
Absence of a backup/recovery mechanism in the repository is reported as NOT VERIFIABLE, not as a vulnerability.
Findings in findings.json are frozen before report generation; the report introduces no additional findings.
